events.title: Commodore 64 released
events.summary: Commodore released the C64 in August 1982 — an 8-bit home computer that became the best-selling single computer model of all time.
events.about: The C64 packed 64 KB RAM, sprite graphics, and a SID sound chip into a sub-$600 package. Millions learned BASIC and 6502 assembly; demo scene coders pushed hardware limits; game developers shipped on cartridge and disk. Its install base made it a first platform for bedroom programmers before the IBM PC dominated.

narrative.whyChosen: The Commodore 64 put programmable computers in tens of millions of homes worldwide.
narrative.whyImportant: It created a generation of developers who learned on real hardware before university or the web.
narrative.problemSolved: Families wanted an affordable computer for games and learning, not a $3,000 business machine.
